A loop is one thing you do again and again that ends in a result outside your head: something booked, sent, paid, bought, filed or published.
Rule: the loop ends in a result that exists outside your head, and an agent can produce that result: a booking, a sent message, a payment, a purchase, a filed document, a published page.
Rule: one set of success tests fits every time the loop happens.
If different occurrences need different rules, the loop is several loops.
A loop that covers three kinds of situations can't be judged by one test, and it takes three times the work to hand over.
The ceiling test
Rule: the level where the agent does the real thing fits within the area's ceiling (protocol section 7).
If the ceiling really applies, keep the loop in your 100, but don't pick it to start.
The success tests then measure the output.
Verbs that pass: book, buy, order, pay, send, reply, schedule, file, submit, renew, cancel, publish, plan and book, collect and send.
Verbs that usually fail: decide, choose, remember, remind, track, monitor, keep an eye on, stay on top of, think about, prepare, review, manage, handle.
Before you leave it empty, ask: would a stranger or another agent confuse this loop with a neighbor in the same area?
Never: restate done when, list steps (those belong in experiment stages), or put evidence or history here.
